family.note: Below the 7500/10000 family-transplant threshold (best guess 7338, LOW confidence) and confirmed a false positive: Shop_UseSelectedItem is an unrelated interactive selection loop (WaitFrames/input-poll/Ability_GetAvailability), sharing only the generic register-shuffle prologue shape with this owner. The real kinship is with games/gs1/src/character_menu/*.c: the very first literal pool word this owner loads is 0x03001f2c (Data_03001f2c), the same InventoryMenuState global build_availability.c/draw_selection_cursor.c/update_selection_icons.c already key off, and this owner directly calls CharacterMenu_BuildAvailability (Func_080a8b10), CharacterMenu_UpdateSelectionIcons (Func_080a9dc4, called twice), and InventoryMenu_ApplyCategoryItemFlags (Func_080a9d3c) -- all three already-named siblings in that same subsystem, immediately below CharacterMenu_DrawSelectionLabels (main:080a8508) in address order.

notes: Reads as the screen-setup routine that runs once a usable item and target category are chosen: sets menu->cursor->state=1 (InventoryMenuIcon.state, offset 5, via the already-typed InventoryMenuState.cursor field), calls Func_080a8914(window,owner,mode), builds the 5-slot usability array via CharacterMenu_BuildAvailability(entries,1,owner), pushes it to the icon row via CharacterMenu_UpdateSelectionIcons(entries), optionally draws an outer window border (Func_08015068) unless mode&0x100 is set, then lists up to 5 available-action text lines (message ids 0xbd5..0xbd9, one per entries[i], stacked at y=40+16*count, falling back to message 0xbd4 'none available' when the array is all zero) -- these five ids sit directly adjacent to draw_selection_labels.c's own Data_00000bdc/Data_00000bda message table, reinforcing the sibling relationship. Refreshes the icons a second time, applies InventoryMenu_ApplyCategoryItemFlags(entries), then reads a still-unnamed u16 at menu+0x220 (immediately before InventoryMenuState.completion_flag at 0x222, not yet a named field) and returns early when it equals 3 (a category that skips the whole stat-preview block below).

The remaining body (reached when the mode&0xff==1 'use' path is taken) draws four page/type tiles via Func_08015280(window,1..4,x=15/19/23/27,row_y,4) where row_y defaults to 7 for mode==1 and 10 otherwise, then a party-comparison flag (compare_mode, computed via the explicit (u32)(-t|t)>>31 zero/nonzero idiom rather than a bare '!=0' -- matching this compiler's idiom for booleans stored to memory rather than branched on immediately) gates a quantity-remaining message (0xafd) and, when mode==1, an icon (Data_080af22c) plus a two-part label (Value_00000afe, Value_00000afe+1) whose glyph addresses sit directly after draw_stat_delta.c's InventoryMenu_IncreaseGlyph/DecreaseGlyph pair (0x080af224/0x080af228), then a 4-iteration loop over party slots reading Runtime_GetObject(owner)+280/+284 (per-slot u8 flags), +72..+86 (four s16 pairs) via Func_080150b0/Func_08015098 at per-slot x=104/112/120+32*i.

Cross-checked the object+72 and object+280 offsets against an independent m2c decompilation of the real reference assembly run through this project's own workbench (tools/compiler -- workbench): m2c's own trace (var_r8_260=sp14+0x48, var_r5_266=sp14+0x118) confirmed +72 and caught a hand-tracing slip in an early pass of this session that had the second base at +160 instead of the correct +280 (0x118); the draft was corrected to +280. m2c's own compiled candidate scored worse on this project's objdiff similarity (71.29%) than the hand-written draft here (76.68%), so the m2c output was used only to verify offsets/algorithm, not adopted as source shape.

This is a class=wrong, non-adopted draft: the algorithm, every call target and its argument order, and every literal constant (message ids, glyph addresses, tile indices, offsets) are reproduced and were independently cross-checked, but candidate_bytes (760) undershoots owner_bytes (768) by one stack slot -- the compiler keeps row_y permanently spilled to its stack home (reloaded at every use) in the reference, while this draft's variable count lets the allocator promote it to a callee-saved register instead, which cascades into different hard-register choices for window/menu/entries-pointer throughout the rest of the function. This is register-allocation noise, not a semantic gap (matched_prefix=7, then continuous small register-role substitutions rather than any missing or extra call/branch). No PERM_GENERAL or hand register-forcing was used, per project constraints; closing this residual would need a further pass isolating exactly which additional local the true source keeps live to force that spill, or a permuter run once that is identified.
